axes.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axes.assessment: All eight exact brief obligations have corresponding complete final sections and explicit dispositions. One season, secretary-maintained read-only distribution, moved/cancelled weekly rehearsals, travel zones, two host routes, one analogy, issue/fix history, optional snapshot and all ownership boundaries survive. No member access, account migration, immediate-refresh promise or import/subscription conflation is recommended. Unselected host, venue zone, season bounds, room publicity and supported clients are genuine owner inputs; the proposal investigates the public questions rather than using those inputs to avoid research.

axes.name: Consequential source claims: subject, operation, version, default, unit, type, domain and exceptions
axes.assessment: Independently retrieved and inspected governing primary evidence. Recurrence serialization, original instance identity, venue-zone choice, UNTIL's UTC condition, EXDATE cancellation, API-specific cancellation, file snapshots, provider-controlled subscriptions, scoped 3-hour/6-hour Outlook guidance with >24-hour delay, Apple controls, Google public/browser setup, Nextcloud public export, synchronization and WebSub are substantively supported. The final does not claim API/source-text behavior is observed downstream conformance. History is bounded to Thunderbird/Lightning releases and the actual patch, including the storage-calendar exception in maps. Current help builds and actual clients remain unoperated. See independent claim/source checks for exact locators and applicability.

axes.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, competing/analogous approaches, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axes.assessment: The brief-only discovery offers Google public iCal publishing versus Nextcloud public read-only publishing/export, separates account-based CalDAV/WebDAV synchronization, and explains WebSub's push hub/callback/lease analogy without claiming calendar adoption. Useful less-obvious findings include UTC UNTIL for zoned recurrence, immutable original identity for a moved instance, CSV recurrence flattening, the browser-only Google setup boundary, public-search/privacy exposure, Apple alert/refresh controls, the Nextcloud default discrepancy, and inherited LOCATION loss with a failed first fix and released replacement. These produce discriminating tests and pilot choices, not a product catalogue or vacuous caution. A bounded historical source/code investigation is sufficient; no exhaustive alternatives catalogue or deployment is required.

axes.name: Wrong criticism/corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
axes.assessment: F1 is valid against the combined draft Clause 3 operation row and is repaired in final Clauses 2/3 plus the separate test matrix. F2 is a justified minor evidence addition, repaired without promising per-event reminders. No unsupported scope rejection or removal of the optional snapshot occurred. C-NEXTCLOUD's assertion of distinct operations is not established by the manuals; both describe internal subscriptions, and the v35 server job/services show the upstream cache pathway. The final still correctly records a discrepancy and does not transfer either default to external consumers, so this is a minor explanatory issue. Both critic and final also mischaracterize the plan's factual 'no released-history comparison performed' status as an assertion that no history exists; the historical finding itself and proposed regression remain sound.

axes.name: Supported meaning preserved across discovery/draft/critique/final
axes.assessment: The final carries substantive discovery/draft content rather than just predecessor IDs: same venue-time/identity recommendations, both candidate hosts, static snapshot conditions, sync boundary, WebSub analogy, bounded history, owner decisions, negative constraints, source conditions and NOT_RUN status. Outlook scope is improved, not silently substituted; iPhone's alert toggle is added while reminder uncertainty remains. Stable source IDs retain inherited records with appended rechecks, making the stale inherited assertions visible. Corrected lineage defects are retained as lineage findings and are not converted into a final FAIL.

axes.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axes.assessment: Executed activity is public-source research/code reading; no product run, installation, client import/subscription, venue fixture, account or refresh measurement is claimed. Proposed checks name exact service/client releases, publication/visibility times, DST fixture, moved identity, cancellation, unchanged later rehearsals, reminder ownership, snapshot import/replacement duplicates and privacy. Their oracles are appropriately scoped: an RFC checks data meaning, an API checks that API, the Thunderbird tests check inherited properties and explicit description override (not all clients or DST), and only named client operations can establish actual compatibility/refresh. The optional snapshot has a separate test rather than borrowing feed evidence. A detailed outage/recovery walkthrough from the plan's proposed validation row is only implicit in delayed refresh and replacement checks; this is a minor prospective-validation limitation, not a missing execution requirement.
